question: In which of the following states of matter do particles possess the highest speed of rapid random motion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Matter exists in three primary states:** solids, liquids, and gases, distinguished by the arrangement and energy of their particles.
 
• In a **Gas**, particles possess the **highest speed of rapid random motion** due to their maximum kinetic energy and weakest intermolecular forces. These particles move freely in all directions at very high velocities.
 
• In a **Solid**, particles are held together by strong intermolecular forces in a fixed lattice. They vibrate about their mean positions, resulting in the **lowest speed of motion**. Hence, this statement is *incorrect.*
 
• In a **Liquid**, particles have moderate kinetic energy and can slide over one another, allowing the liquid to flow. Their speed is **higher than solids but lower than gases**. Hence, this statement is *incorrect.*
